findings.title: Appraisal by AI: Model-driven victim prioritization in the VOLTA infostealer
findings.summary_md: Cisco Talos researcher Ryan Fetterman published the original analysis on October 31, 2026. The self-deleting malware, self-named VOLTA-AUTODOXER, collects credentials, sessions, cryptocurrency wallets, and then uses LLMs to profile victims and rank assets. Talos notes it did not confirm in-the-wild usage.

findings.title: Spooky New Infostealer Malware Uses AI to 'Autodox' Victims
findings.summary_md: WIRED reported on October 31, 2026, exclusively referencing the Talos finding. The malware defaults to Claude Opus 4.6 via OpenRouter, with fallbacks to Kimi K2 and Gemini 2.5 Flash. Fetterman told WIRED that Volta has not been tracked in active campaigns.

findings.title: Malware called Volta-Autodoxer uses AI to build a dossier on its victims
findings.summary_md: Startup Fortune summarized the Talos disclosure on October 31, 2026, describing how Volta feeds stolen profiles to AI models like Claude Opus 4.6 through OpenRouter to automatically profile and rank victims.
